title: Compare House Prices neighborhood smoothing on authorized competition data
summary: Actual-data verified for one recorded run: global log-price mean versus fixed neighborhood smoothing on five unchanged random folds of the official Ames training file. Smoothing lowered mean fold natural-log RMSE from 0.3991 to 0.2687; exact official scoring parity remains unverified.
split_definition: Five shuffled random folds with seed 17; each row validates once; all log-price category means fit training rows only.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.13 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64, in one local CPU run on 2026-10-26. Other Python versions and platforms are not covered by this receipt. Set private input/output environment variables as documented before execution.
steps: Inspect the official data, rules and evaluation pages, obtain authorized train.csv (and optional test.csv) yourself, and keep them outside Git/public.
Use the pinned package and private environment variables; preserve the same five random folds and fixed smoothing weight five.
Inspect public aggregate diagnostics and your private once-only OOF residuals; explain log and dollar units and retain worse changes.
Optionally compare a notebook run with the script run exactly, and validate any private submission locally without uploading.
limitations: One recorded run on one machine (Python 3.12.13, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-26); a notebook run of the same package matched it exactly but other environments are untested.
Neighborhood smoothing lowered natural-log RMSE on all five random folds (mean 0.2687 versus 0.3991); this is a validation-fold result, not a Kaggle leaderboard score, and no submission was made.
Official indexed overview confirms log-price RMSE but does not specify logarithm base; direct page bodies were unavailable and exact scoring implementation/base parity remains unverified.
Random folds do not establish spatial or temporal transfer.
Mean fold natural-log RMSE is distinct from pooled OOF RMSE; dollar MAE is diagnostic only.
Row residuals and submission IDs remain private; public slices below ten rows are suppressed.
Traced allocations are not RSS; no learner compute budget measured.

project.outcome: Explain train-only neighborhood smoothing with fixed random folds and residual diagnostics in log and original units.
prerequisites: Run a local Python script and set private environment variables.
Explain natural logarithms, RMSE and a training/validation split.

access.instructions: Inspect https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/data and current rules yourself; obtain authorized train.csv and optional test.csv privately. Follow docs/house-actual-data-setup.md; no automatic acquisition or submission.
access.authorization: Recorded run used the official, unmodified train.csv and test.csv downloaded on 2026-10-26 through the Kaggle API by the repository owner's Kaggle account after accepting the competition rules. Readers must obtain their own copy: sign in, inspect and accept the current competition rules yourself, and download the official files; this site does not distribute them.

project.baseline: Fit the global training natural-log price mean inside each fixed random fold.
project.controlled_change: Compare neighborhood means with five fixed pseudo-examples on exactly the same folds; retain worse outcomes.
diagnostics: Does the neighborhood change help consistently across the same five unchanged random folds?
How do log residuals and original-dollar errors differ across fixed price bins and seen/unseen neighborhoods?

troubleshooting.symptom: Missing authorized data or access failure
troubleshooting.recovery: Stop before running: inspect the official data, rules and evaluation pages, accept the rules yourself if eligible, and obtain your own copy. The recorded receipt does not grant access.
Use the setup recovery table, restore pinned files and rerun into a new private output directory; never publish raw errors or inputs.
